rounds.text: Network People Services Technologies Ltd demonstrates exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 87% over the trailing twelve months [E16] and a five-year profit growth CAGR of 107% [E17]. This aggressive expansion is supported by a robust balance sheet that is nearly debt-free [E56], with borrowings reduced to just Rs 7 Cr [E35] and a strong current ratio of 7.42x [E34]. The company’s ability to generate superior returns is clear, as its 19.7% ROCE [E12] and 15.0% ROE [E13] significantly outperform sector benchmarks [E10, E9]. Furthermore, the completion of capital expenditure, indicated by CWIP falling to zero [E36], suggests the company is well-positioned to capitalize on its new capacity without further heavy investment. Institutional confidence is reflected in the positive money flow [E40] and the increasing stake held by domestic institutions [E39]. Conceded: the company faces valuation headwinds with a high P/E of 77.6x [E1], negative operating cash flow [E30], and a decline in operating margins [E26, E27].

NPST is currently trading at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E ratio of 81.14x compared to a sector benchmark of 18.61x [E6]. This aggressive pricing is further underscored by a P/B ratio of 8.23x against a sector average of 1.29x [E7], and an EV/EBITDA of 45.83x, which is more than triple the sector benchmark [E11]. The company’s internal cash generation is a major concern, as evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -45 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -93 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is deteriorating, with operating margins contracting by 10 percentage points over the last three years and 5 percentage points in the most recent quarter [E26, E27]. The company is also struggling with ballooning working capital requirements, as evidenced by an increase in working capital days from 31.1 to 140 days and high debtor days of 195 [E64, E62]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong historical sales and profit growth [E14, E17] and maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio [E33]. Despite these growth metrics, the current market price implies an earnings growth rate of 27%, which exceeds the base case assumption of 18% [E43], leaving the stock vulnerable to any deceleration in performance.

The bear’s focus on valuation multiples ignores that NPST is fundamentally outperforming its sector, justifying a premium for its superior growth profile [E6, E7, E11]. While the bear highlights high P/E and P/B ratios, it fails to account for the company’s exceptional profitability, with an ROE of 9.27% and ROCE of 12.32% significantly outpacing sector benchmarks of 5.44% and 5.84% respectively [E9, E10]. Conceded: the company reported negative operating and free cash flow in March 2026 [E30, E31, E32]. However, this must be weighed against the company’s robust liquidity, evidenced by a current ratio of 7.42x and a near-debt-free status that provides a massive buffer for operational fluctuations [E33, E34, E56]. Regarding margin contraction, the company’s long-term compounded profit growth of 107% and sales growth of 66% demonstrate that it is successfully scaling despite short-term margin volatility [E14, E17, E28]. Finally, the bear’s concern over working capital ignores that the company has completed its capex cycle, with CWIP down 100%, signaling that new capacity is ready to drive future earnings [E36].

Conceded: the company displays strong historical top-line and bottom-line compounding [E14, E17], and its current ratio stands at a comfortable 7.42x alongside low debt [E33, E34, E56]. However, the bull's reliance on sector-beating ROE and ROCE [E9, E10] ignores that these metrics are optically inflated relative to the heavy valuation multiples being paid, with P/E at 81.14x versus a sector benchmark of 18.61x and EV/EBITDA at 45.83x against 12.95x [E6, E11]. The claim that completed capex through zero CWIP will drive earnings [E36] completely glosses over the alarming reality that operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs -45 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs -93 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32], destroying cash conversion [E30]. Furthermore, pointing to long-term growth to dismiss margin contraction ignores the immediate deterioration where operating margins fell by 10 percentage points over three years and 5 percentage points in the recent quarter [E26, E27]. Finally, the bull brushes off working capital risks, yet the company suffers from high debtors of 195 days and working capital days that ballooned from 31.1 days to 140 days [E62, E64].
